Hi Vanessa / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — AtlasCare is excited to move the POC forward. Before legal signs the SOW we need a couple of operational confirmations so our security and procurement teams can close their review: 

1) No-training / no-improvement: we need a signed attestation that data sent during our POC will not be used to train or improve Redwood models (including any downstream variant training by subprocessors). A PDF attestation is fine.

2) Subprocessor routing & proxies: one of our concerns is intermediary vendors (EdgeMirror Inc.) that will proxy requests from our client application to Redwood. Can you confirm:

   - where any subprocessors operate (country/region), and,

3) KMS / key residency: AtlasCare requires customer-managed keys or an onshore KMS path for any artifacts that would constitute derived outputs or telemetry. Can you confirm options here and any limitations for POC workloads?

Attachments requested: attestation PDF + subprocessor inventory + a one-page KMS summary would be ideal.

Summary answers (high level):
- No-training: Redwood will provide a signed attestation that AtlasCare interactions during the POC will not be used to train or improve public or internal models. - Subprocessors & proxy handling: EdgeMirror (you called them out) is treated as a transport proxy in our default flow. We do not persist customer payloads at EdgeMirror beyond short-term buffering necessary for request delivery. We maintain a subprocessor inventory with residency flags; attached is the CSV snapshot. High-level: most infra subprocessors operate in us/eu regions; none of the listed subprocessors will persist data for model training during the POC.

- KMS / residency: For POC we can offer an onshore KMS wrap for artifacts and telemetry; see the attached "kms-onshore-summary.txt" for the approach (customer-managed keys via AWS KMS in us-east-1, policy excerpt). If AtlasCare needs HSM-backed keys or an HSM appliance, we can scope that under Dedicated or Private deployments.

Hi Marta — following up with the technical confirmations Kimberly asked for.

1) EdgeMirror: per our operational logs and contract with EdgeMirror they act as a TCP/HTTP proxy only for the POC flow. They perform transient buffering (seconds-level) and intrinsic request routing. They do not write raw payloads to long-term storage in any S3 bucket. We have the contractual SLO that prohibits using POC data for model training.

2) Export / SFTP: We can schedule a nightly SFTP export of interaction snapshots to an AtlasCare-controlled SFTP endpoint in us-east-1. That export includes metadata only (interaction IDs, timestamps) unless you request full transcript snapshots; we will only export full transcripts under explicit request and retention settings you approve.

3) KMS: For the POC we will use a customer-provided CMK in AWS KMS (us-east-1). Attached summary includes the key policy snippet and steps to provision and rotate. If AtlasCare wants an HSM-backed solution we can escalate and provide Dedicated/Private pricing.

Attachments: kms-onshore-summary.txt (excerpt), subprocessor-inventory-20261106.csv

If you'd like, I can jump on a 20-minute call to walk through the inventory and export lane. Otherwise Kimberly and Vanessa can complete DocuSign and we can ship the attestation.
